A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SADs study and contain readable experiments, figures, equations, Table 1 and Appendices A–C. Content can be reliably matched despite reformatting and reordered proofs.

before.justification: v1 reports original sphere and rank-one simulations, architecture comparisons, and image-generation experiments on MNIST, CelebA-HQ and CIFAR-10, including numerical Wasserstein results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical outcomes, including the architecture comparison in Figure 5 and image benchmarks in Figures 8–9.

M1.justification: The average output geometry, eigenvector-based SAD ranking, DSM networks and orthogonal Wmin/Wmax transformations remain unchanged. Corrections to analytical geometry formulas do not establish a changed modeling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same rank-one Gaussian distributions, sphere subspaces, MNIST, CelebA-HQ and CIFAR-10. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The architecture comparisons retain iDDPM, iDDPM with area resampling, DiT/2 and DiT/4. The standard-basis experiments and Wmin, identity and Wmax comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains the same architectures, learning rates, batch sizes and iteration budgets. Wasserstein metrics and 64D projection counts also remain. Appendix A's explicit training/testing sample counts clarify documentation rather than establish changed sampling or splits.

E4.justification: The resampling ablation, patch-size comparison, SGD-dynamics simulation, image-adaptive geometry example and MNIST sample analysis are retained. The exchange of Figure 5 and Figure 6 numbering introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 removes Appendix A's statement that all experiments were repeated five times with different seeds and Figure 9's description of averages over five independent runs. Five-run reporting for Figure 2 and mean-plus-standard-error reporting for the architecture comparison remain. This is reduced reporting, not evidence of fewer runs.

E6.justification: Plotted scores, curves and sample panels are unchanged; Figure 8 retains MSW2 values 0.61, 8.78 and 8.52. However, Table 1's caption newly reports that DiT/4 converges more slowly per iteration than DiT/2; v1 explained the doubled iteration budget through approximate runtime matching.

T1.justification: The transformer proof corrects the shared-bias covariance contribution from an identity matrix to an all-ones matrix (v1 C.6; v2 C.3). Theorem 2's proof explicitly distinguishes the orthostochastic feasible set from its doubly stochastic relaxation and establishes feasibility of the extremizers. v2 also adds independence in Lemma 2, restricts linear geometry recovery to nondegenerate probes, and narrows Theorem 1's covariance assertion from near optimality to optimality.

C1.justification: The central contribution—predicting directional preferences from geometry at initialization—remains. However, v2's Discussion drops v1's claim that the bases define the order in which data features are learned, presenting the contribution as an empirically validated predictive framework instead.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly describes the Markov argument as heuristic and proposes that geometry captures architectural invariants persisting through optimization. It removes the explanation that identity and Wmax already have high alignment and may not differ significantly, and drops the proposed discriminative–generative trade-off. The principal small-scale and foundation-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A now explicitly specifies 10k training and 10k testing samples, while removing the 128GB RAM specification. Table 1 revises the explanation for the unchanged DiT/4 budget from approximate runtime equalization to slower convergence and inexpensive additional iterations.

R1.justification: The shortened related-work discussion removes detailed homogeneity and forward-pass contrasts with Jacobian-based approaches. Citations to Mohan et al. (2020), Nakkiran et al. (2020) and Wen et al. (2024) disappear, and the MNIST database reference is replaced by LeCun et al. (1998). The principal NAD and GAHB positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively edited and condensed. Motivation moves earlier in Section 3, subsections are renamed, related-work and limitations prose is shortened, broader-impact material is reorganized into the Discussion, and a separate Impact Statement appears. Appendix C places proposition proofs before theorem proofs.

P2.justification: The predominantly single-column presentation becomes a two-column conference layout with new headers, extensively resized and repositioned figures, revised captions and a reformatted Table 1. All nine figures remain, with the former Figures 5 and 6 exchanging numbering; the presentation changes do not constitute new experimental displays.

improvement.justification: The corrected transformer covariance and explicit relaxation argument in Theorem 2 improve mathematical reliability, while removing the feature-learning-order claim better calibrates the conclusion. These targeted gains outweigh the limited loss of seed-reporting detail and the caveat about identity versus Wmax comparisons. The overall improvement is modest.
